traps: ZEXPORT, ZEXTERN, FAR and local stand before or inside the declarators: a parser without the macros of include/zmconf.h reads local uLong FAR mod_base as a declaration of a variable named FAR or mod_base of type local
OF((args)) wraps parameter lists: zm_adler OF((uLong adler, ...)) is a prototype, not a call
the definitions in c/zmini.c are K&R style (parameter types declared between ) and {): legal in C90, gone in C23
ZEXPORT expands to __stdcall only on Windows with ZMINI_DLL, which is defined only for a shared build: the macro value depends on platform and BUILD_SHARED_LIBS
include/zmini.h is one C header compiled by both languages: extern "C" guards make it valid C++, it is still C
cpp/detail.h is C++ (namespace, template) with a .h extension; c/zutil.h and include/*.h are C
#define local static leaks into every C++ file that includes zmini.h; checksum.cpp includes the standard headers first for that reason
add_library(zmini zmini.c) has no STATIC or SHARED: its kind follows BUILD_SHARED_LIBS
